name: Seccomp boundary
description: Seccomp BPF filters limit the host syscalls Firecracker can issue. Loaded per-thread immediately before that thread runs guest code (VMM thread before vCPU dispatch; vCPU threads before KVM_RUN; API thread before HTTP server start). The primary defense-in-depth between guest-controlled code and the host kernel — assumes the guest has rooted the VMM and tries to expand to the host.

name: Default seccomp filter (embedded)
description: Firecracker embeds compiled seccomp BPF filters at build time. Source JSON lives at resources/seccomp/<arch>_musl.json in the repo. The build step uses seccompiler-bin to compile JSON → bitcode → embed in the binary. Production deployments use these defaults — overriding is for experimental targets or quick mitigations only.

name: Custom seccomp filter (--seccomp-filter)
description: Override the embedded default with a custom seccompiler-bin-compiled file via --seccomp-filter <path>. Use cases: GNU libc experimental builds, debug builds that need extra syscalls (fcntl F_GETFD), emergency mitigation of an unallowed syscall in production. CAUTION: misconfiguration can disable the boundary entirely.

name: --no-seccomp (development only)
description: Disables ALL seccomp filtering. Marked NOT FOR PRODUCTION. Useful for quickly prototyping Firecracker changes that use new syscalls. Often paired with --gdb-socket since GDB-required syscalls are blocked by default filter.

name: Debug-binary seccomp gap
description: Debug binaries and experimental GNU targets ship WITHOUT default seccomp filters installed — the build process skips embedding them since they're not for production. Implication: never run debug builds in untrusted environments. Verify with `firecracker --version` (release vs debug suffix).

name: Seccompiler-bin
description: Compiles seccomp filter JSON into serialized BPF bitcode consumed by Firecracker. CLI: `seccompiler-bin --target-arch <arch> --input-file <json> --output-file <bin>`. Library API also exposed for in-process compilation. Filters use a custom JSON schema with thread-name-keyed objects, each containing default-action + filter rules (syscall-name + arg conditions).

name: Thread-keyed seccomp filter structure
description: JSON filter file is keyed by thread-name string (vmm, api, vcpu) — Firecracker installs the matching policy per thread before that thread starts running. Lets the API thread allow HTTP-server syscalls (accept, recvfrom) that vCPU threads must NOT have.

name: BPF bitcode serialization format
description: Compiled filters are stored as bitcode (not raw BPF instructions). Firecracker deserializes the bitcode at startup and installs via prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER, ...). Bitcode format isolates the BPF compiler from runtime — Firecracker doesn't need a BPF assembler embedded.

name: Kernel support policy
description: Each Firecracker release commits to supporting specific HOST and GUEST kernel versions for a minimum of 2 years. ≥2 major versions of each kept simultaneously. New version added → oldest deprecated and removed in the next release after its end-of-support date. Going outside the matrix may work but is not validated by CI — frequent source of obscure boot/runtime failures.

name: Host kernel matrix
description: Currently supported host kernels: v5.10 (since v1.0.0, end-of-support 2024-01-31) and v6.1 (since v1.5.0, end-of-support 2025-10-12). 4K page size only. Other kernels may run but are unvalidated.

name: Guest kernel matrix
description: Currently supported guest kernels: v5.10 (since v1.0.0, EOS 2024-01-31) and v6.1 (since v1.9.0, EOS 2026-09-02). Validation guest configs at resources/guest_configs/ in the repo. Microvm-specific kernels are vended by Amazon Linux at github.com/amazonlinux/linux under microvm-kernel-* tags.

name: Minimal guest boot Kconfig set
description: Smallest guest-kernel CONFIG flags needed to boot. Initrd boot: CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD=y + (aarch64 CONFIG_VIRTIO_MMIO=y | x86_64 CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y). Block-device boot: CONFIG_VIRTIO_BLK=y + (x86_64: CONFIG_ACPI=y, CONFIG_PCI=y, CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y). Optional console: CONFIG_SERIAL_8250_CONSOLE=y + CONFIG_PRINTK=y.

name: ACPI vs MPTable boot transition
description: x86_64 only. Firecracker historically used MPTable + virtio-mmio.cmdline kernel-param hack to enumerate devices. Modern path: ACPI (CONFIG_ACPI=y, CONFIG_PCI=y in guest) supersedes both. Firecracker still supports legacy mode for back-compat — but if the guest kernel has BOTH enabled, devices are enumerated TWICE and the second init fails (harmless dmesg warnings; devices still work).

name: VirtIO over PCI (--enable-pci)
description: x86_64 optional. --enable-pci flag at firecracker startup switches all VirtIO devices to PCI transport (vs default MMIO). Higher throughput + lower latency per device. Requires PCI-enabled guest kernel + REMOVING `pci=off` from boot_args (Firecracker auto-adds it when PCI is disabled).

name: Default kernel boot args
description: Default boot_args: `reboot=k panic=1 nomodule 8250.nr_uarts=0 i8042.noaux i8042.nomux i8042.dumbkbd swiotlb=noforce`. Each flag tuned for fast boot or for the i8042-driven shutdown path. + `pci=off` appended unless --enable-pci. User can override entirely via /boot-source.boot_args.

name: Snapshot compatibility across kernel versions
description: Snapshot save and restore hosts must agree on enough kernel features for the snapshot's encoded device/CPU state to be replayable. Cross-kernel-version restore is best-effort — see fc-docs-snapshot-support 'Snapshot compatibility across kernel versions' section. Plan production deployments to use the same host kernel.

name: SECURITY.md disclosure policy
description: Firecracker's responsible-disclosure policy. Vulnerability reports go to firecracker-security@amazon.com (NOT public GitHub issues). Disclosure timeline aligns with AWS-wide policy. Reproducers and CVE assignment handled by the maintainer team.
